title: Grade 4 Science — Tue, May 26
description: Rocks & Minerals — Day 2 of 5: Properties of rocks
subject: science

questions.question: What is hardness of a rock?
options: How resistant it is to being scratched
questions.explanation: Hardness = scratch resistance. Diamond is the hardest; talc is the softest. Measured on Mohs scale (1–10).

questions.question: Which rock property describes how light reflects off its surface?
questions.explanation: Luster = how light reflects. Rocks/minerals can be metallic (shiny like metal) or non-metallic (dull, waxy, glassy).

questions.question: Rock texture refers to:
options: The size and arrangement of grains or crystals
questions.explanation: Texture = grain size and arrangement. Granite has visible crystals; obsidian is glassy smooth; sandstone has sand-sized grains.

questions.question: A rock that can be scratched by a fingernail is:
questions.explanation: A fingernail has hardness ~2.5. If it scratches a rock, the rock's hardness is less than 2.5 — very soft (e.g., talc, gypsum).

questions.question: Which property describes whether a rock lets water pass through it?
questions.explanation: Permeability = ability to let water (or other fluids) flow through. Sandstone is permeable; granite is not.

questions.question: Granite has large visible crystals. This tells us the magma cooled:
questions.explanation: Slow cooling underground allows large crystals to grow. Fast cooling (like lava) makes tiny or no crystals.

questions.question: Obsidian is a shiny, glassy igneous rock. Why is it glassy?
options: Lava cooled so fast no crystals formed
It is made of glass minerals
questions.explanation: Obsidian forms when lava cools extremely fast — crystals have no time to form, giving a smooth glassy texture.

questions.question: A rough, sandy-feeling rock is likely:
questions.explanation: Sandstone has sand-sized grains cemented together — it feels rough and grainy, unlike smooth marble or glassy obsidian.

questions.question: Which rock property would you test to decide if a rock is good for making a kitchen countertop?
questions.explanation: Countertops need to resist scratching from knives and pots. Hardness is the key property — granite (very hard) is ideal.

questions.question: Colour alone is NOT a reliable way to identify a rock because:
options: Same mineral can appear in many colours; different minerals can look the same colour
questions.explanation: Quartz comes in purple (amethyst), pink (rose quartz), clear, and more. Colour varies with impurities so it is unreliable alone.

questions.question: A rock has metallic luster. What does that mean?
options: It shines like a metal surface
questions.explanation: Metallic luster = the surface shines like polished metal. Examples: pyrite (fool's gold), galena.

questions.question: Which property makes marble a good building and sculpture material?
options: It is hard and takes a smooth polish
questions.explanation: Marble is hard and polishes to a smooth, shiny finish — ideal for statues, temples, and flooring.

questions.question: Sandstone is used for building because it is:
options: Easy to cut and shape, moderately durable
questions.explanation: Sandstone is relatively easy to cut and shape while still being durable enough for buildings — common in traditional architecture (e.g., Red Fort).

questions.question: If rock A scratches rock B, which is harder?
questions.explanation: The rock that does the scratching is harder. Harder minerals scratch softer ones — this is how the Mohs hardness test works.

questions.question: Summary: which set of properties helps identify a rock?
questions.explanation: Rock identification uses multiple properties: colour (guide), texture (grain size), hardness (scratch test), luster (light reflection), permeability. No single property is enough.
